DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

The combination of progressive gait disturbance requiring wheelchair assistance, a history of urinary incontinence, and recent onset of dysarthria (speech slurring) in a 54-year-old male is highly suggestive of a rapidly progressive neurodegenerative process affecting both upper and lower motor neurons. Given the severity of the gait impairment and the specific pattern of symptom progression, I need to confirm if you have noticed any muscle weakness in your arms or legs, or if your speech difficulty is accompanied by difficulty swallowing or choking?
